newsitem.title: UK: Wheat extends a rally, oil prices ease.
newsitem.headline: Wheat extends a rally, oil prices ease.

text.p: Chicago wheat futures returned to $4 per bushel on Wednesday after a recent dip as they extended a rally based on hopes of a pick-up in U.S. exports.
A gain of some 15 cents from the end of last week showed that, despite bumper harvests around the globe, grain markets are still volatile as world stocks remain low.
The key December wheat futures position on the Chicago Board of Trade gained 6-1/2 cents to touch $4.00, a price last seen on November 29.
Traders said CBOT wheat futures were higher on news India may become an importer of wheat rather than an exporter and on hopes for a sale of U.S. wheat to Pakistan and perhaps Russia, traders said.
"There's a chance of doing the Pakistan business, the prices are in line for the U.S. to do it," a trader said.
Pakistan is expected in the market on December 22 for 270,000 tonnes of Australian or U.S. white wheat.
Also there was some bullish input that Iraq is now clear to sell oil on the world market and talk that it will therefore be importing wheat, the traders said.

Oil prices extended losses on Wednesday following news that Iraq was coming back and also, of more immediate impact, data showing that depleted U.S. heating fuel stocks are at last starting to fill up.
Benchmark Brent Blend crude from the North Sea for January delivery traded as low as $22.40 a barrel, down from Tuesday's close at $23.29.
After the market closed on Tuesday, the American Petroleum Institute (API) said stocks of U.S. crude oil, distillates -- mostly heating oil -- and gasoline rose last week.
Copper and aluminium prices pushed higher on Wednesday on bouts of shortcovering and ended near day's highs.
Three-months copper finished the London afternoon kerb session at $2,163 per tonne, up $27, after early short covering gains met little in the way of selling.

News the Dutch Bureau of Statistics admitted supplying flawed data on copper flows through Rotterdam, which cleared up a puzzle about the possible existence of substantial hidden stocks, was a background factor.
Aluminium also ended firmer, up $23.50 at $1,527, after a bout of shortcovering pushed up values in the afternoon.
Precious metals markets were not much changed. London's benchmark March robusta coffee contract was just $2 down on the day at $1,262 a tonne.
